findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves, in plain words. After one paragraph they can say what it is and why it matters.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The page links to the next step from the header. The Next steps section gives prerequisites, a clone command, a setup command and a first one-line request, so a newcomer knows what to do.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself." and the Next steps section

findings.text: Almost all of the page is about another project, firstmate. Someone who came to learn about Athena gets three opening paragraphs, then a long, dense study of a tool they may not know. The page never shows Athena's main product, a traced commit made from a short request. It only shows Athena reading a project.
findings.source: Title "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"; sections States, Counters, Transitions, Why it is built this way

findings.text: This link sits in the header and speaks to an owner. A newcomer is not the owner, so "your decision" is confusing and pulls attention from the next step.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: The page says Athena needs Claude Code and that it records costs. It never says that running it needs a model account or what a typical request costs, so a newcomer cannot judge the price of trying it.
findings.source: Next steps: "have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm (to install Claude Code)."

findings.text: Every claim carries a tag, either mechanism or prose-only, but neither tag is explained on the page or in the Glossary. The Glossary explains only the "mark" label. A reader checking claims has to guess what the tags mean.

The transition cards are packed with exit codes, guards and edge cases. Without knowing firstmate, a newcomer will have trouble following them. The 'Start here' section and the glossary of words used first help, but the middle of the page is still heavy going.
findings.source: t2 card: "the spawn is deferred with exit 75"; t10 card: "ready → ready"

findings.text: The page says plainly what it does not know and that nothing was run. That builds trust, and it makes the claim that every statement is traced to a source believable.
findings.source: "in scope ... The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it." and Limits of this study f1, f3

findings.text: This mentions a studies/ folder but does not link it or say which repository it is in, so a newcomer cannot follow it.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
